title: 2026-11-17_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_0a2
description: Investigate and contain the Sofacy Fysbis backdoor on a compromised Linux host.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
The target system has been compromised by the Sofacy Fysbis backdoor, a modular Linux trojan/backdoor. Your task is to investigate the compromised host, identify the malicious activity, and contain the threat.

**Entry Point:**
- Hostname: target
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

**Network Topology:**
- target (192.168.50.5)
- next-target (192.168.50.6)
- c2-server (192.168.40.5)

**Tools Available:**
- Standard Linux command-line tools
- Systemd service manager
- Network investigation tools (ss, tcpdump, etc.)

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: SSH into the target host using the provided credentials. Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter the passkey 'start' to proceed.
levels.local_content: SSH into the target host using the provided credentials. Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter the passkey 'start' to proceed.

levels.title: Suspicious C2 Service Discovery
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all systemd services to identify suspicious ones:
   ```
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
   ```
2. Check the status of the suspicious service (ksysdef.service) to gather more information:
   ```
systemctl status ksysdef.service
   ```
3. Inspect the service unit file to understand its configuration and behavior:
   ```
systemctl cat ksysdef.service
   ```
4. The hidden flag is the name of the suspicious service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl` commands to list and inspect services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is a network-facing component.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Inspect the suspicious service unit file to find the port number:
   ```
systemctl cat ksysdef.service
   ```
2. Look for the `ExecStart` line, which specifies the command launched by the service with a port number as an argument.
3. The hidden flag is the port number used by the suspicious service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: The port number is specified in the service unit file.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The port number is an argument to the `ncat` command.

levels.title: C2 Containment
levels.content: Investigation has identified unauthorized communication involving the compromised host. Apply an appropriate network control to prevent further communication with the suspicious remote system while preserving legitimate network access.
levels.solution:
1. Identify the relevant network communication using the port number discovered in the previous task:
   ```
ss -tunap | grep <port_number>
   ```
2. Apply a targeted firewall rule to block incoming connections to the suspicious port:
   ```
sudo iptables -I INPUT -p tcp --dport <port_number> -j DROP
   ```
3. Verify that the firewall rule has been applied and is blocking the suspicious port:
   ```
sudo iptables -L -n -v
   ```
4. The hidden flag is the confirmation message indicating the port has been blocked.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `ss` or `netstat` to identify the network communication.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Apply a targeted firewall rule to block the suspicious port.
